frames.observation: The exact Tideglass body is visible in settled Crab_Idle at 58 HP. Its teal shell, eye stalks, legs and copper-and-ivory pincers form a coherent silhouette under the retained native purple wizard hat.

At the native attack transition the crab remains present behind the foreground hero and impact particles. Occlusion limits fine leg inspection, but no detached authored section or vertex burst is visible.
During Crab_Attack1 at close range, the shell, eyes, pincers and visible legs articulate together. The native hat stays positioned above the authored head.
The last Crab_Attack1 sample shows the crab returning toward its slot with the complete authored silhouette intact. Native damage presentation affects the hero and does not hide the target.
The final pass frame returns to Crab_Idle with the same readable shell, face, limbs, pincers and native hat. This proves sampled recovery, not every crab proficiency.
The ordinary no-focus player attack begins with the exact target intact at 58 HP and settled in its enemy slot.
The native Damaged trigger begins under a bright impact effect. The target is mostly occluded, so this frame establishes the causal transition without supporting fine surface review.
During Crab_Hit, the authored body recoils behind the foreground hero. The visible hat, shell edge, legs and pincer remain aligned despite the close overlap.
The crab has recovered to a stable idle at the measured 56 HP. The machine record establishes the same-target ordinary 58 to 56 outcome.
A subsequent native Crab_Attack2 begins with the crab advancing from its slot. Shell, face, pincers, legs and hat remain one readable character.
Midway through Crab_Attack2, the target is close to the hero and partly covered by native light and particles. The visible authored sections stay connected without sampled stretching.
At the end of Crab_Attack2, the crab is again readable behind the hero with its complete silhouette intact. Native freeze effects apply to the hero and limit color comparison.
The final ordinary-attack frame shows the exact body back in Crab_Idle at 56 HP with no renderer loss, viewport clipping or visible floor fall-through.
The explicit fixture-death capture begins with the exact target intact at 56 HP. This is pre-death appearance evidence before the separate KillSingle action.
The native Death trigger begins under the explicit fixture impact. The bright effect and foreground hero obscure the target, so no detailed deformation claim comes from this frame.
Crab_DeathDirect begins with the authored crab raised behind the hero. The shell, legs and pincers remain coherent as the animated death starts.
During Crab_DeathDirect the crab falls back toward the floor with its authored body intact. The controller records m_DoRagdoll=false, so this is animated death evidence rather than a ragdoll claim.
The authored body lies in a coherent settled pose at the enemy slot during the completed death capture. No sampled mesh explosion, detached authored section or floor fall-through is visible.
The native victory and loot surface now obscures most of the scene. The target remains partly visible behind it, so this frame supports presence only and not fine corpse inspection.
The exact renderer is still active, enabled and visible behind the loot panel. UI and depth blur prevent a detailed late-pose verdict.

The final requested frame completes the 120-frame fixture capture with the renderer still active, enabled and visible behind the loot surface. No corpse lifetime beyond this sampled window is claimed.

requirements: All 21 referenced original PNGs were inspected at original resolution before assigning this reviewed status.
The ordinary no-focus gameplay claim is limited to the same-target HP change from 58 to 56; the separate KillSingle fixture is not ordinary lethal evidence.
The death claim is an animated Crab_DeathDirect path with m_DoRagdoll=false, not a ragdoll claim.
The exact renderer remained active, enabled and visible in all 360 retained frames; selected originals support visual conclusions only for their sampled views.
Native UI, attack effects, foreground hero overlap, loot overlay, depth blur and camera movement limit fine surface, culling and corpse inspection.
